html:
The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India, adopted on 26 November 1949 and in force from 26 January 1950, now Republic Day. It is the longest written national constitution in the world.

It was written by the Constituent Assembly, elected before independence, which met from 1946 to 1949 amid the violence of Partition. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the drafting committee, working from a first draft by the civil servant B. N. Rau, and Nehru wrote its statement of aims. Much of its machinery came from the British Government of India Act 1935.

What it set up:

  • A federal parliamentary republic with universal adult suffrage from the start, in a country where most people could not read.
  • Fundamental rights that courts enforce, and "directive principles" the state should aim for.
  • The abolition of untouchability, and reserved seats and jobs for Dalits and tribal peoples.
  • A secular state, with the word "secular" added to the preamble in 1976.

It is easy to amend and has been changed more than a hundred times. In the Kesavananda Bharati case of 1973 the Supreme Court ruled that Parliament cannot change its "basic structure". It was put to its hardest test in the Emergency of 1975 to 1977, when Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties, and it survived.
sum: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of India, adopted on 26 November 1949 and in force from 26 January 1950, now Republic Day. It is the longest written national constitution in the world.
